subject: Post-call: evaluation runbook + minimal dataset requirements for Halcyon Labs
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schultz <hannah.schultz@halcyonlabs.com>, Dr. Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@halcyonlabs.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: evaluation runbook + minimal dataset requirements for Halcyon Labs

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — great to meet the Halcyon team. Below is a concise recap and the suggested next steps to get a Redwood-hosted, customer-specific evaluation up and running as quickly as possible.

Quick recap from the call:
- Goal: Validate model fit for clinical note summarization + triage suggestions against your internal annotation set.
- Primary constraints: PHI-containing examples (need secure upload), target latency 250ms p95, and want a reproducible scoring rubric for tracking regressions.
- Timeline: pilot evaluation in ~2 weeks, full benchmark within 6 weeks depending on dataset handoff.

Recommended models to include in the benchmark (start small):
- RW-7B-instruct (fp16) — baseline production candidate for balanced quality/latency.
- RW-3B-q4 — low-cost variant for throughput comparisons.
- Redwood-Chat-2B (instruction-tuned) — to test conversational prompts and triage phrasing.

Artifacts attached and links:
- redwood_eval_runbook_v1.pdf (attached) — runbook with dataset schema, scoring scripts, and expected outputs.
- halcyon_minimal_dataset_sample.csv (attached) — a 20-row sample CSV showing columns we need.
- Drive folder with full templates: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qAredwood-eval-docs-example

Minimal dataset format (required fields) — see attached CSV sample for examples:
- id (string): unique id for example
- source_text (string): full clinical note or excerpt (max 6k chars)
- prompt_type (string): "summarize" | "triage" | "extract"
- gold_output (string): reference summary / triage label / extraction result
- label_type (string): "summary" | "categorical" | "span"
- metadata_tags (string): optional; fields like dept=ER; redaction_flag=true

Scoring criteria (baseline rubric):
- Summarization: ROUGE-L and a human pass/fail on critical info (presence of diagnosis, medications, allergies) — target: ROUGE-L >= 0.52 and critical-info recall >= 0.90 for pilot pass.
- Triage: macro F1 on the 4-class triage label set (low/medium/high/urgent) — pilot target F1 >= 0.78.
- Extraction: exact-match and span IoU with a small allowance; exact-match >= 0.85.

Quality/regression monitoring notes:
- We will run the same prompt sets and scoring scripts as part of the evaluation; Redwood Optimize can produce delta reports between model versions and highlight regressions at the prompt-example level.
- We'll add a small set (~100) of 'sentinel' examples (edge cases) to track regression sensitivity.

Security / upload suggestions:
- For PHI, we recommend using Redwood Private or a presigned, short-lived S3 upload to our staging bucket; we can also accept an SFTP transfer. See attached redwood_privacy_upload_instructions.txt.
- We'll provide a signed NDA addendum if required before transfer (we can coordinate via your legal team).

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Halcyon: send a 1–2 week sample export (CSV/JSONL, 200–500 rows) with PHI redacted or on a secure transfer method.
2) Redwood: stand up an isolated evaluation run in your account or in our Private environment; run the 3-model pilot and return a scoring report + example-level diffs.
3) Joint: schedule a technical run-through with Karthik (solutions) and Tessa (CS) to finalize prompts and scoring scripts.

Possible dates for run-through: Aug 12, 13, or 16 — please indicate availability.

If anything above needs correction, say so — otherwise we'll assume the sample export and privacy option are the next items.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: evaluation runbook + minimal dataset requirements for Halcyon Labs

Thanks Vanessa — this is very clear and helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we hand over anything: 

1) PHI/PII: most of our notes contain names, MRNs, and dates. We need assurance around retention and audit logging. Is the short-lived S3 + Redwood Private option fully isolated (no shared logs)? Can we get a short data flow diagram for the pilot?

2) Redaction: we'd prefer to avoid doing heavy redaction on our side. Does Redwood have an automated redaction step you recommend that we can run prior to upload? If so, what is the false-positive/negative behavior we should expect?

3) Timeline: we can provide a 250-row export by EOD Friday (Aug 13) if the upload process is confirmed. After that, what's the typical turnaround for the scoring report?

Also, Dr. Lee asked whether we can add a small set of clinician-reviewed edge cases (about 50) with richer annotations (reasoning notes). Any concerns about format? He can export as JSONL with an additional "rationale" field.

I'll loop in our security contact if needed — but for now, please send the succinct answers and the data-flow link.

Best,
Hannah Schultz
Product Manager, Halcyon Labs
hannah.schultz@halcyonlabs.com

(Attachment: halcyon_sample_export_inquiry.txt — short list of fields in our export)

Hannah — thanks for the questions, great items. Short answers below; happy to follow up with your security lead.

1) Isolation & audit logs: Redwood Private gives you an isolated control plane and no shared customer data pools. For the hosted pilot (if you prefer), we can stand up a customer-isolated staging bucket and provide audit logs for object access — I attached high-level data flow in the redwood_privacy_upload_instructions.txt. If you want, Karthik can prepare a 1-page diagram for your security team.

2) Automated redaction: we do offer an optional redaction preprocessor as part of the evaluation runbook. It flags likely PHI (names, MRNs, SSNs, dates) using pattern- and ML-based detectors. Typical behavior: very low false positives for numbers/IDs, names can be trickier (we recommend a brief human-spot check on 200 rows). If you prefer, we can run the redaction step on our Private staging and give you an auditable diff.

3) Turnaround: once we receive the 250-row export on a secure transfer, typical pilot run (3 models, scoring + human spot-check) is 3 business days. We'll deliver a PDF report plus a CSV with example-level metrics and the failing examples.

Edge cases: JSONL with an extra "rationale" field is fine — we'll wire that into the human evaluation tab in the report. Please include a schema line at the top or send a sample first row.

Next actionable items I will take care of:
- Karthik will assemble the 1-page security/data-flow diagram and send it to you by EOD today.
- Tessa will add the evaluation job to our queue and create the scaffolding for the pilot.
- If you confirm the S3 presigned upload or Redwood Private, we'll share the upload instructions and a short NDA addendum link.

Proposed quick sync: Thu, Aug 12 at 10:00 AM PT (15 minutes) to confirm upload path and finalize the sample schema. If that works for you, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
